articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Native Multimodal Reasoning and Extended Context
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5, featuring natively fused vision, audio, and text reasoning in a single architecture rather than stitched-together modules. The model supports a 1M-token effective context window and demonstrates significant gains on agentic coding benchmarks, with early enterprise adopters reporting 40%+ improvements in multi-step task completion rates.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Ultra Tops New ARC-AGI-2 Benchmark
articles.summary: DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Ultra became the first model to surpass 80% on the ARC-AGI-2 abstract reasoning benchmark, a suite specifically designed to test novel pattern generalization that prior models struggled with. The result has reignited debate about how close frontier models are to general reasoning versus sophisticated pattern matching on increasingly broad training distributions.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces 'Claude Codebase Agent' for Autonomous Repository-Scale Engineering
articles.summary: Anthropic launched a specialized agentic product built on Claude that can autonomously navigate large codebases, plan multi-file refactors, write and run tests, and submit pull requests with human-in-the-loop review gates. Early benchmarks on SWE-Bench Verified show it resolving over 70% of real GitHub issues end-to-end, pushing the frontier of AI-assisted software engineering.

articles.title: Figure and BMW Expand Humanoid Robot Deployment to Full Assembly Line
articles.summary: Figure announced that its Figure 02 humanoid robots are now operating across an entire sub-assembly line at BMW's Spartanburg plant, moving beyond the initial pilot phase. The robots handle parts transfer, fastening, and quality inspection using on-board vision-language models, with BMW reporting a 25% throughput improvement and a path toward three-shift autonomous operation.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics Atlas Now Performs Adaptive Manipulation in Unstructured Warehouse Environments
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics released a technical update showing its electric Atlas robot autonomously picking, placing, and palletizing irregularly shaped packages in a live DHL warehouse using a new sim-to-real reinforcement learning pipeline. The system adapts on-the-fly to novel objects not seen during training, representing a major step toward general-purpose robotic manipulation in logistics.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm-Class N14P Process Node
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed volume production has started on its N14P (1.4nm-class) process, utilizing backside power delivery and gate-all-around nanosheet transistors. The node delivers roughly 20% speed improvement and 30% power reduction over N2, with Apple and NVIDIA among the first customers expected to tape out designs for late-2026 and early-2027 products.

articles.title: Microsoft and Quantinuum Demonstrate Fault-Tolerant Logical Qubit Operations Below Error Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Quantinuum published results showing sustained fault-tolerant operations on 12 logical qubits with error rates below the threshold needed for practical quantum error correction, using Quantinuum's H3 trapped-ion system and Microsoft's new qubit virtualization layer. This milestone marks a credible entry into the early fault-tolerant era and opens the door to first useful quantum chemistry simulations.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Begins: First Compliance Audits Target Foundation Model Providers
articles.summary: The European AI Office initiated its first formal compliance audits under the EU AI Act's general-purpose AI provisions, targeting several major foundation model providers operating in Europe. Companies must now demonstrate systemic risk assessments, red-teaming documentation, and compute reporting, setting a global precedent for binding AI regulation that is being closely watched by US and UK policymakers.
